results.title: NVIDIA H100 pricing: rental rates and total cost | Hivenet
highlights:
NVIDIA H100 pricing depends on the GPU variant, the number of GPUs you rent, and what the service includes. On October 19, 2026, Lambda listed a single H100 PCIe instance at $3.29 per GPU-hour and a single H100 SXM instance at $4.29. Modal listed H100 SXM5 GPU time at $0.001097 per second, approximately $3.95 per hour, with other resources charged separately. The provider links and billing details are in the comparison below.

These are dated examples, not a market-wide minimum or a guarantee of available capacity. A useful comparison starts with the complete bill for a workload that meets your requirements. This guide explains the units, purchase options, and calculations to check before renting or buying H100 hardware.

...

An H100 GPU-hour measures one GPU allocated for one hour. Eight GPUs running for ten hours represent 80 GPU-hours, even though only ten hours have elapsed. If a provider quotes the whole instance, multiply that instance rate by time once. Multiplying it by the GPU count again would double-count the hardware.

...

H100 PCIe, SXM, and NVL are not interchangeable configurations. NVIDIA's H100 specifications list 80 GB of GPU memory for SXM and 94 GB per GPU for NVL, with different power and interconnect specifications. A provider's 80 GB PCIe listing is another configuration to identify explicitly. Ask whether an offer supplies a complete GPU, a partition, or a multi-GPU system.

...

The prices listed below were checked on October 19, 2026 and are in USD. They illustrate different configurations and service models. They do not establish equivalent performance, availability, or a cheapest-provider ranking. Confirm taxes, region, account terms, and the launch price before committing.

results.title: H100 price per hour, October 2026: 11 clouds compared · ClearCompute
results.author: Ronit Ahuja
highlights:
The short answer

On 5 October 2026, one H100 80GB SXM listed at $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand across nine clouds, and the Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80. Five specialist clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. The hyperscalers charged $6.88 (AWS), $11.06 (Google Cloud) and $12.29 (Azure), though a three-year commitment brings them down to between $2.97 and $5.40. For an inference server, four things matter as much as the rate: the smallest unit you can rent, egress, billing increments and how fast the price is moving.

## H100 prices on 5 October 2026#

## Prices rose this autumn#

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on 1 October: H100 by 17% ($3.85 to $4.50), H200 by 20% and B200 by 19%.
- AWS announced a 15% rise in EC2 Capacity Block prices from 7 October, taking a P5 H100 from $5.19 to $5.97 per GPU-hour.
- Verda's H100 went from $3.37 on 22 September to $3.77 on 5 October, up 12% in 13 days, according to the Wayback Machine's captures of its price page.

Any price survey goes stale within weeks, this one included. For today's number, live trackers such as gpufinder.dev, which polls 22 vendors every hour, and SkyPilot's GPU Compass are better sources. A survey is more useful for explaining what the number buys.

results.title: H100 rental price — what clouds charge per GPU-hour
results.author: Daniel Okafor
highlights:
The H100 rental price depends on the provider and on how you rent. On the providers’ own pricing pages, one Nvidia H100 ranged from $1.78 per GPU-hour, the lowest live ask on the Lium marketplace on October 19, 2026, to $11.06 on demand on Google Cloud, checked October 2. Among the clouds, CoreWeave spot was about $2.46, and Lambda and Nebius listed on-demand H100s at $3.99 and $4.50. These prices change often; the full, regularly re-checked list is on our cloud GPU price tracker.

...

## Per instance or per GPU

Clouds publish H100 prices in two ways. Some list a price for a single GPU: Lambda shows its H100 SXM at $3.99 “/GPU/HR”, and Nebius lists the HGX H100 per GPU-hour. Others sell whole machines, usually eight H100s with CPUs, memory and local storage, and quote the machine’s hourly price. AWS, Google Cloud and CoreWeave do this. To compare the two, divide the instance price by the number of GPUs in it. CoreWeave’s 8-GPU HGX H100 instance lists at $49.24 an hour in North America, which works out to $6.155 per GPU-hour.

...

- Google Cloud’s a3-highgpu-8g (8 H100s) comes with 208 vCPUs, 1,871 GB of memory and 6,000 GiB of Local SSD, all included in its hourly price.
- CoreWeave’s HGX H100 instance includes 128 vCPUs, 2,048 GB of system RAM and 61.44 TB of local storage.
- Lambda lists its on-demand H100 SXM configuration with 208 vCPUs, 1,800 GiB of RAM and 22 TiB of SSD.

A higher per-GPU figure can include more CPU, memory and disk. When you compare offers, compare the whole configuration, not the GPU line alone.

It also matters which H100 you get. Nvidia sells the H100 SXM with 80 GB of memory and 3.35 TB/s of memory bandwidth, and the H100 NVL with 94 GB and 3.9 TB/s. Rental listings usually name the form factor (SXM, PCIe, HGX); our AI chip catalog has the specs.

...

The same GPU costs different amounts depending on the commitment.

On-demand is pay-as-you-go: you start and stop instances and pay by the hour at the list price. All of the per-GPU figures from Lambda, Nebius and Google Cloud in the table below are on-demand.

...

## H100 prices on the providers’ pages

All figures below were read on each provider’s own pricing page on October 2, 2026, except the Lium row, which was read on October 19, 2026. Lium is a marketplace where the hosts set their own prices, so its figure is the lowest live ask at the time of reading and changes as machines are added and removed. Per-GPU-hour values for instance prices are the instance price divided by eight.

| Provider | Offer | Billing | Listed price | Per GPU-hour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lium | H100 80GB HBM3 (SXM), marketplace, lowest live ask | On-demand, billed per second | from $1.78 per GPU-hour (checked October 19, 2026) | $1.78 |
| CoreWeave | HGX H100, 8 GPUs, North America | Spot | $19.71 per instance-hour | $2.46 |
| Lambda | H100 SXM 80 GB | On-demand | $3.99 per GPU-hour | $3.99 |
| Nebius | HGX H100 | On-demand | $4.50 per GPU-hour (effective October 1, 2026) | $4.50 |
| AWS | p5.48xlarge Capacity Block, US East (N. Virginia) | Reserved, paid up front | $41.528 per instance-hour | $5.191 |
| CoreWeave | HGX H100, 8 GPUs, North America | On-demand | $49.24 per instance-hour | $6.155 |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g, Iowa (us-central1) | On-demand | $88.49 per instance-hour | $11.06 |

Prices move in both directions and sometimes within days. Nebius’s table shows the HGX H100 at $3.85 per GPU-hour in its previous on-demand column and $4.50 in the column effective October 1, 2026. AWS’s P5 Capacity Block rate changes on October 7. Treat the table as a dated snapshot and check the cloud GPU price tracker for the current figures, which also cover Azure, RunPod, DigitalOcean, Crusoe, Hyperstack and other providers.

## What the hourly price leaves out

A GPU-hour price is rarely the whole bill.

- Tax. Lambda states its prices are “plus applicable sales tax/VAT/GST.” Most list prices are quoted before tax.
- Data transfer. CoreWeave says it charges “no ingress, egress, or transfer fees,” and Lambda advertises no egress fees. On clouds that do charge for data transfer, the charge is billed separately from the GPU-hour.
- Storage. Local SSD is part of several of the instance prices above, but persistent or network storage for datasets and checkpoints is priced separately.
- Operating system and software. AWS bills the Capacity Block operating system fee separately from the reservation fee, and lists different OS fees for Linux, RHEL, SLES and Ubuntu Pro.
- Region. Hyperscaler prices are per region. The AWS and Google Cloud figures above are for US East (N. Virginia) and Iowa respectively; other regions list different rates.

results.title: What a million tokens costs on a rented H100 or B200 — Die Brief
results.author: The Die Brief Desk
highlights:
Nebius posts 4.50 dollars an hour for an H100 and 8.50 for a B200 from 8 October 2026. Lambda posts 3.99 and 6.69 on its instance page. Neither page prices a million tokens.

...

What an H100 hour has cost Grey is an H100 SXM5 hour: $4.85 from November 2023 through July 2024, then $3.50 in September 2024. Copper is an H100 NVLink hour: $2.95 through May 2026, $3.85 from June, $4.50 from 1 October 2026. They are different offers. The gap is empty on purpose.

...

Nebius prints the rates in its document Compute pricing in Nebius AI Cloud. The page says on-demand prices for B300, B200, H200, and H100 changed on 1 October 2026, and that from 8 October 2026 the preemptible price on several of those platforms is a dynamic spot rate, displayed as a floor. The dollar figures on that page are before tax. The billing unit is one second and the pricing unit is one hour, so thirty minutes is half the hourly rate. A stopped virtual machine is not charged for the GPU. The bars are the on-demand rates read on 10 October 2026. The 8 October note on that page is a preemptible floor, and it is not drawn. The line above the bars is what an H100 hour has cost across the months a posted rate could be read.

...

Lambda's instance page, opened the same day, lists the chip, the onboard memory, the vCPUs, and a price per GPU-hour, plus applicable tax. The B200 SXM6 row with 180 GB and 208 vCPUs is 6.69 dollars. The H100 SXM row with 80 GB and 208 vCPUs is 3.99 dollars. The A100 SXM row with 80 GB and 240 vCPUs is 2.79 dollars. The page groups further rows under smaller instance sizes. B200 SXM6 appears again at 6.79, 6.89, and 6.99 dollars, next to 104, 52, and 26 vCPUs. H100 SXM on those rows is 4.09, 4.19, and 4.29 dollars. An H100 PCIe row with 80 GB and 26 vCPUs is 3.29 dollars. A GH200 row with 96 GB is 2.29 dollars. Under the B200 section the page says the instances start at 6.69 dollars, and it says the part offers up to three times the training and fifteen times the inference of H100. It does not say how many tokens that hour produces.

...

An H100 hour has not moved in one smooth line, and the two rates on the chart are different offers. The SXM5 pay-as-you-go hour was $4.85 from November 2023 through July 2024, and $3.50 on 15 September 2024. The later NVLink hour was $2.95 from October 2025 through May 2026, $3.85 from 1 June 2026, and $4.50 from 1 October 2026. The months between September 2024 and November 2025 are left empty. The posted offer changed, and those in-between months were not in the copies read for this brief. A third quote, $2.118 for the GPU alone with the processor and memory billed beside it, is not drawn.

The useful update is the dated move on the Nebius page itself. From 1 October 2026 the on-demand H100 line goes from 3.85 to 4.50 dollars, the H200 line from 4.50 to 5.40, the B200 line from 7.15 to 8.50, and the B300 line from 7.85 to 9.50. Those four pairs are on one document, with the old rate left in place under a "before" heading. Lambda's instance rows do not carry a date. The 6.69 and 3.99 dollar figures are what that URL showed on 10 October 2026, and a revision should open the URL again rather than treat them as a contract.

results.title: Lambda GPU Cloud 怎么选？A100、H100、B200 和按分钟计费讲清楚 | 智机玄同
results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月9日 4 分钟阅读
highlights:
资料核查日期： 2026年10月9日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

...

你选择一个已经定义好的 GPU 实例，CPU、RAM、SSD 也跟着实例规格一起确定。

例如截至 2026-10-09，Lambda 官网公开的单 GPU 实例包括：

- A100 PCIe 40GB：$1.99 / GPU 小时
- A100 SXM 40GB：$1.99 / GPU 小时
- H100 PCIe 80GB：$3.29 / GPU 小时
- H100 SXM 80GB：$4.29 / GPU 小时
- GH200 96GB：$2.29 / GPU 小时
- B200 180GB：$6.99 / GPU 小时

这些不是裸 GPU 价格。

实例还带 CPU、系统内存和 SSD。

所以它和 Vast.ai 那种“不同主机自己报价”的 Marketplace 不能只按一列 GPU 单价硬比。

## 按小时展示，但实际按分钟

Lambda 官方 Billing 文档说明：

On-Demand Cloud 用小时价格展示，但按一分钟增量计费。

计费从实例启动并通过健康检查以后开始，一直到你终止实例。

这里“终止”很重要。

机器即使什么也没算，只要仍然在运行，就继续计费。

所以 Lambda 这类标准 VM 最简单的省钱办法仍然是：

不用就关，不要把 H100 当远程桌面一直挂着。
